name: Secret Hitler
summary: Hidden-role deduction game where liberals and fascists battle to enact policies and elect or eliminate Hitler.
rules_text: Players are secretly assigned as liberals (majority), fascists, and one Hitler. Fascists know each other except Hitler may not know them in large games. Players rotate as President. President nominates a Chancellor (not previous government), all vote Ja/Nein simultaneously. If majority Ja, President draws three policy cards (6 liberal, 11 fascist), discards one face-down, Chancellor enacts one of the remaining two, discarding the other. Other discards are hidden. If vote fails, election tracker advances; after three failures a random top policy enacts. Enacting fascist policies unlocks Presidential Powers: peek deck, investigate party, call special election, or execute a player. After three fascist policies, fascists win if Hitler is elected Chancellor. Liberals win if Hitler is executed or five liberal policies pass. Fascists win with six fascist policies.
rating_reason: Hidden team policy game with voting and deck
reasons: capability: conditional_subsequence: the step list is flat: a whole BLOCK of steps cannot be chosen instead of another block. This is NOT a limit on conditional scoring or conditional updates: a single step can carry a `when` condition and a single operation an `if`, both arithmetic, so 'the poisoner scores if the choices match, otherwise the chooser' is fine
